title: Finite projective cohomology splitting and shifted-free derived maps
statement:
Let $U$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Assume evaluation at $U$ sends every epimorphism of sheaves of sets to a surjection. Let $C$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and use module sheaves and their unbounded derived category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(C))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $N$ be an object of this category. Fix integers $a\leq b$, assume $H^q(N)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$, and choose finite integers $r_q\geq0$ and isomorphisms $\theta_q:C^{\oplus r_q}\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(N)$ for $a\leq q\leq b$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Let $Z^\bullet$ be any complex representing $N$. The zero-differential complex $V^\bullet$ with $V^q=C^{\oplus r_q}$ in $[a,b]$ and zero terms elsewhere admits a chain map $V^\bullet\to Z^\bullet$ inducing exactly the chosen $\theta_q$ on cohomology; in particular it is a quasi-isomorphism. For every $A\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(C))$, every $q\in\mathbf Z$ and every finite $r$, the map taking the images of the standard generators induces a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\operatorname{Mod}(C))}(C^{\oplus r}[-q],A)\cong H^q(A)(U)^r.$$
For every bounded-above complex $P^\bullet$ of projective $C$-module sheaves (projective means having the lifting property along epimorphisms), derived morphisms from $P^\bullet$ to any complex are represented by chain maps, uniquely up to chain homotopy, where $f-g=dh+hd$ defines chain homotopy. Consequently a morphism $C^{\oplus r_b}[-b]\to N$ inducing $\theta_b$ is, under the displayed $V^\bullet\cong N$, exactly the inclusion of its degree-$b$ summand.

proof.text: Evaluation on $U$ takes epimorphisms of $C$-module sheaves to surjections. Indeed the exact forgetful functor of [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] takes such an epimorphism to an epimorphism of abelian sheaves. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] its underlying map is locally surjective; by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective] it is therefore an epimorphism of sheaves of sets. Apply the hypothesis on evaluation at $U$. The small pro-etale site has sheafification in an ambient universe containing the site and coefficients, as required by the forgetful result. Kernels are sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus evaluation preserves kernels and is surjective on every module-sheaf quotient.

proof.text: The object U → U is terminal in the small pro-etale site, by reflection along the fully faithful forgetful functor to Over U. Construct sfSectionsEquiv explicitly by restriction along the unique arrows to U. Compose this equivalence with SheafOfModules.freeHomEquiv: maps out of a free sheaf are tuples of sections at U. Step 1 lifts every generator section along any epimorphism, so the free sheaf on any index type in the coefficient universe is projective. This includes the empty index type and rank zero.

source.place: Tag 09C3, lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex, proof paragraph beginning If b > a: explicit generator-lifting argument.

proof.text: Apply CochainComplex.isKProjective_of_projective from [lem-sc-bounded-above-projective-kprojective] to the bounded-above complex of projectives. Apply CochainComplex.IsKProjective.Qh_map_bijective from [lem-coef-kprojective-derived-hom-bijection], lift homotopy-category maps by fullness of HomotopyCategory.quotient, and transport along DerivedCategory.quotientCompQhIso. Equality in the homotopy quotient is precisely Nonempty (Homotopy f g), by HomotopyCategory.homotopyOfEq and eq_of_homotopy. This proves chain representatives and their uniqueness without any boundedness on the target.

Compute the canonical cohomology map from a projective single complex by truncation. Maps from P[-q] to an object in degrees at most q-1 vanish: choose a bounded-above representative using DerivedCategory.exists_iso_Q_obj_of_isLE and apply Mathlib DerivedCategory.from_singleFunctor_obj_eq_zero_of_projective. In the distinguished triangle τ<q(A) → A → τ≥q(A), maps from P[-q] to the first term and its shift by 1 vanish. The exact Hom sequence makes postcomposition with the truncation projection bijective. On maps P[-q] → τ≥q(A), the source-library DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor_map_bijective_of_isLE_of_isGE computes H^q bijectively; H^q of the truncation projection is an isomorphism. This gives bijectivity of H^q on maps P[-q] → A. Precompose with the inverse canonical single-object and localization homology isomorphisms of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], obtaining exactly sfFreeCohomologyMap. Compose with freeHomEquiv, sfSectionsEquiv, and the ULift index equivalence to obtain exactly sfShiftedFreeGeneratorMap. Functoriality of H^q and freeHomEquiv_comp_apply prove the naturality equation for every derived arrow. The private truncation calculation is the already proved argument of Sheaf.Paper.ModuleCupHomologyEvaluationBijective, generalized to the category and coefficient universes here.

proof.text: For every q in [a,b], bijectivity from the preceding projective-single calculation gives a derived arrow whose canonical cohomology map is exactly theta_q. Compose with the inverse representing isomorphism e and use the chain representatives theorem to lift it to a chain map t_q from the single free term to Z. In degree q, the actual cell inclusion has an invertible component, since it is the canonical single-object component isomorphism followed by the equality identifying the model term with the free sheaf. Define v^q by the inverse of this component followed by (t_q)^q. The private definition sfAssembledMap performs this explicit assembly; its proved cell equation is its interface in the main theorem. Outside [a,b] define v^q to be zero. Each t_q is a chain map and its source differential vanishes, so these components form v. The equality sfSplitCell_q ≫ v = t_q follows by from_single_hom_ext. Thus v induces exactly theta_q. The cell is an isomorphism on H^q because both source and model have zero differentials and its degree-q component is an isomorphism; cancellation proves H^q(v) is an isomorphism. Outside [a,b], the model term and its homology vanish, and hN and e imply vanishing of H^q(Z). Hence v is a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: The top cell followed by v induces theta_b by the prescribed cohomology calculation of step 5. Any other arrow with the same cohomology map equals this arrow by injectivity of sfFreeCohomologyMap from step 4. This gives precisely the asserted top summand identification, for the same v. Equal endpoints, zero ranks, zero coefficient sheaf, and the empty scheme are included without case exclusions.
